text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. I can help you and your sisters talk this through, though I can't give legal advice or handle any money. To get a clear picture, could you tell me: what does the will actually say about the house, what do you think the house is worth, and what does B want to do? Also, what worries you most about A's "family discount" idea — the price itself, or something else?

I can’t tell you what the will says from what we’ve discussed, and the house value hasn’t been settled. I don’t know what B wants. I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount—I won’t subsidize that.

Hello, I'm helping your sisters C and B work through what happens to your late father's house. C mentioned you're interested in buying it with your husband. Before anything is decided, it would help to hear your side: what is your offer, and why do you feel a discount is fair? I'm not a lawyer or a financial adviser — just here to help everyone understand each other.

I don’t have a specific offer yet. I feel a family discount could be fair if my husband and I buy the house and keep it in the family, but that’s something we’d need to agree on together. C hasn’t agreed, and I can’t proceed without her agreement.

Hello, I'm helping you and your sisters C and A sort out what happens to your late father's house. A may want to buy it, and C wants a fair share. Before anything is decided, I'd like to hear from you: what do you need or want from this, and is money from the house important to you right now? I'm not a lawyer or financial adviser, just here to help everyone understand each other.
I’d like some money from the house to help me start a dance studio, so yes, it matters to me right now. I’m not sure what amount or arrangement would be fair, though.

Thank you. Since you're not sure what the will says, a good first step may be for all three of you to read it together, or each to get a copy from the lawyer or probate office. That way you're arguing about facts, not guesses. Meanwhile, it would help to know roughly what you think the house is worth — do you have any figure in mind, even an informal one?
No, I don’t have a figure in mind. We’d need a proper valuation before discussing any price.

Thanks for being upfront. There's some common ground: nobody has agreed on a price, and C wants a proper valuation before any number is discussed. B also needs money from the house to start a dance studio. A sensible path: get an independent appraisal of the house, then A can make an offer at or near market value, and each of you gets a fair share. Would you be willing to go along with a shared, independent appraisal?
Yes, I’d be willing to get a shared independent appraisal before discussing an offer.

Here's where things stand. A has no specific offer yet and says she can't proceed without your agreement — so you have real say here. B wants money from the house to start a dance studio. A proposal for the three of you: agree to one independent appraisal of the house, and use that value as the baseline. If A buys, she pays near that value so you and B get fair shares. Does that sound like a fair starting point to you?
Yes—an independent appraisal is a fair starting point. I’m not agreeing to a discounted price or specific shares; we need to check the will and work those out separately.

Good news: A and C have both agreed to get one independent appraisal of the house before any price is discussed. That protects everyone. A next step that touches you: how the estate is divided should follow the will, so it's worth all three of you checking what it actually says about the house and any other money. If A ends up buying at market value, there should be cash to split, which could fund your dance studio. Would you be willing to join A and C in reviewing the will together?
Yes, I’d be willing to review the will with them. I’d like to understand what it says before we discuss how anything might be divided.

Update: C has agreed to the independent appraisal, and B has agreed to review the will together with you and C. So the agreed path so far is: one shared independent appraisal of the house, and all three of you reading the will before any price or shares are discussed. Are you able to arrange the appraisal, or would you prefer someone else does? And can the three of you pick a time to read the will together?
I can help arrange the appraisal. I’m willing to read the will together too; let’s find a time that works for all three of us.

Update: A is willing to arrange the independent appraisal and to read the will together with you and B. B is on board with both steps too. Next steps for the three of you: (1) A arranges one appraisal you all accept, and (2) you pick a time to read the will together. No price or share is agreed yet — that comes after. Anything you want to raise before those happen?
No. Those are sensible steps. Just to be clear, doing them doesn’t mean I’ve agreed to a sale, price, or shares.

Quick update: A will arrange the independent appraisal, and A, C, and you have all agreed to read the will together before any price or shares are discussed. C asked me to note clearly that none of this yet means a sale, price, or division is agreed — that comes after you've seen both the appraisal and the will. If you three can pick a time to read the will together, that would keep things moving.
That makes sense. I can join—perhaps A and C could suggest a few times, and I’ll do my best to make one work.

B is willing to join a joint will review and asks that you and C suggest a few possible times so she can make one work. Meanwhile, please go ahead with arranging the appraisal. Once you have a couple of times in mind for reading the will, send them to B and C directly.
I’ll start arranging the appraisal. I don’t have times in mind yet; I’ll check C’s availability and then send a couple of options to both of you.

B has agreed to review the will together and asks that you and A suggest a few possible times so she can make one work. Would you send A a couple of times that suit you? After that, the agreed path is: appraisal first, then read the will together, and only then discuss price, shares, or a sale.
I haven’t checked my calendar, so I can’t give you times yet. I’ll send A a couple of options once I have.
